relations.note: Apep obstructs Re’s barque and is repeatedly repelled and rendered powerless.

relations.myth: Nightly attack on the solar barque
relations.note: Apep blocks Re’s nocturnal passage until divine agents immobilize and pierce him.

relations.myth: Repeated confrontations during Re’s nocturnal journey
relations.note: Apep obstructs the barque and is bound, attacked, and dismembered.

relations.myth: Apep’s birth from Re’s discarded cord
relations.note: Apep forms from Re’s umbilical cord after Neith casts it into Nun.

relations.myth: Binding Apep in the seventh hour
relations.note: Isis uses effective speech from the barque’s prow to deprive Apep of strength.

relations.myth: Binding Apep in the seventh hour
relations.note: Selket binds Apep’s head with a lasso after his strength is neutralized.

relations.myth: Binding Apep in the seventh hour
relations.note: The Eldest Magician joins Isis in neutralizing Apep’s strength.
Atum confronts, controls, and repels coiled Apep to ensure Re’s progress.
Seth spears or otherwise repels Apep while defending Re’s barque.

relations.myth: Destruction of serpentiform enemies at Edfu
relations.note: Horus destroys enemies whose cosmic identity is assimilated to Apep.
relations.source: Great Horus Myth and Edfu ritual scenes

relations.myth: Apep’s birth from Re’s discarded cord
relations.note: Neith casts Re’s umbilical cord into Nun, where it becomes Apep.
Apep emerges in Nun from Re’s discarded cord; Nun is not clearly a father.
Aker guards or restrains Apep’s limbs in creation and overthrowing material.
Re as the Great Cat cuts the hostile serpent beside the ished tree.
Apep is declared Osiris’s enemy, and his destruction protects Osirian renewal.
Plutarch reports a learned tale calling Apopis the brother of Helios.
Apopis wages war against Zeus, who ultimately defeats him.
Osiris supports Zeus in war against Apopis and is adopted as Dionysus.
